data.narrative:
GrayMatter Robotics is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised over $70M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 private same-stage, same-sector comparables (Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity) supplemented by a broader universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable across the robotics sector.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the last post-money valuation of $300M and applying a typical 1.9x step-up multiplier for Series B advancement, yields $570M. Peer-median analysis across the 3 closest comparables produces $1.8B, with individual valuations ranging from $1.6B to $2.0B. The disparity between methods reflects variance in comparable selection and the limited precision of early-stage peer matching in a nascent sector.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $484M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $1.2B. The wide spread—approximately 4x from low to high—reflects material uncertainty around which peer cohort most accurately reflects GrayMatter's competitive positioning and near-term growth trajectory. Key sensitivities include further operational de-risking between now and Series C, market adoption rates for deployed systems, and relative performance versus the identified peer set on unit economics and revenue visibility.
